case.case_title: Dissanayake, Attorney-at-Law on Behalf of K.M. Lai v. Sujeewa, Sub Inspector of Police, Meetiyagoda Police Station and Others
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports (1998) 2 Sri L.R. 413

clause.text: No person shall be arrested except according to law and must be informed of the reason.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the arrest of the petitioner was lawful and whether he was informed of the reason for his arrest in accordance with Article 13(1) of the Constitution.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed he was unlawfully arrested while sleeping in his house close to midnight on 02.06.1996 without proper legal basis and was not informed of the reason for his arrest.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents argued the petitioner was arrested on 03.06.1996 at 12:15 a.m. based on a complaint of threatening bodily harm, and that the petitioner was informed of the reason for his arrest.
key_facts: Petitioner was asleep in his house when police allegedly arrested him close to midnight on 02.06.1996.
Respondents claimed arrest occurred at 12:15 a.m. on 03.06.1996 after dispersing an unlawful assembly.
Petitioner was taken to police station and later admitted to hospital unconscious.
Petitioner’s version of arrest time and place was supported by his mother’s affidavit.
Respondents’ version of arrest timing and circumstances was found incredible by the court.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court interpreted Article 13(1) as requiring that any arrest must be lawful and the person arrested must be informed of the reason for the arrest. The court emphasized the importance of the timing and circumstances of the arrest to determine legality.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found the petitioner’s version credible that he was arrested unlawfully while sleeping in his house, not at the scene of the complaint as claimed by respondents. The respondents’ version was rejected as incredible. Therefore, the arrest did not comply with the legal requirements of Article 13(1).
principles_established: Arrest must be according to law and the arrested person must be informed of the reason.
Credibility of evidence is crucial in determining legality of arrest.
Unlawful arrest violates fundamental rights under Article 13(1).

outcome.holding: The court held that the arrest of the petitioner violated Article 13(1) of the Constitution as it was unlawful and the petitioner was not properly informed of the reason for arrest.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Compensation of Rs. 50,000 payable by the State, Rs. 5,000 costs from the State, and Rs. 5,000 compensation payable personally by the 1st respondent.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(1) was central to the court’s determination that the petitioner’s arrest was unlawful because it was not conducted according to law and the petitioner was not properly informed of the reason, leading to a violation of fundamental rights.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner’s version that he was arrested while sleeping in his house was credible and supported by his mother’s affidavit; the respondents’ version was rejected as incredible.
